pillar_reactions.evidence: Understood and agreed with no questions: 'When it comes to the training and the mobility, do you feel like, yeah, that makes sense? And I see myself doing that? Yeah.' Later, asked which part stood out, he named form: 'probably the form factor is most important for me right now, at this moment, but long-term, I think all of them are equally important.'

Agreed and volunteered his own view, mildly against the rep's framing: the rep said Trevor does not focus on calorie counting, and the prospect replied 'Actually, I believe that it was one of the success, key factors of success. I mean, counting.' The rep then conceded that Trevor does implement counting for overweight clients.

This is the pillar he pushed back on and it decided the call: 'I have the doubts about how it will actually work online, not on the spot correction. Okay, no, no, you're doing this wrong, just, you know, keep your leg a little bit further or something... I'm pretty sure it will be easier for the trainer to see and for me to adapt to the tips, if it's in person.' Also: 'that actually, that's the thing we are talking about right now is probably my biggest question mark.'

anchors.raw: The one month of try with an in-person trainer here in Warsaw is about 250 euro.
anchors.note: The deciding number. He framed it purely as downside exposure — 'if it doesn't go, it's only 200 euro, you know?' — against roughly 1,000 for a month of Trevor. The rep answered 'and if this doesn't go, it's only a thousand', which restated the gap rather than closing it.

anchors.raw: although I think it is, obviously it's worth the six, or if you would tell me 10,000 euro, would also say, okay, it's obviously it's worth. If it's, if it brings you health for next five years, obviously it's worth 10,000 euro or even more. No questions about it, but still there is the question of rates of the return.
anchors.note: He accepted the value at nearly double the asking price and still refused. This proves the loss was not a value objection at all — it was a risk-of-fit objection dressed as price, and the rep kept answering the price.

anchors.raw: I run a business where I'm selling a pretty expensive stuff for, for, you know, people listening to music at home and, and, you know, clients visit us and obviously they, they can afford this and even the more expensive stuff. It's not about this, it's about the amount of money they are okay to spend for this activity.
anchors.note: He diagnosed his own objection in his own professional language — willingness-to-allocate rather than capacity. The rep agreed with the framing but never used it to reposition the category budget.

unmet_demand.want: On-the-spot, in-person form correction during the movement rather than asynchronous video review
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme is built on filmed workouts reviewed within 24 hours. He stated the specific mechanism he wanted and why the offer does not deliver it: 'we learn a movement, and training one, two movements during this lesson. And then I just work on it at home.'

unmet_demand.want: A low-cost way to test whether the coaching relationship works before committing six months and 5.2k
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No trial tier exists. The rep improvised a one-month entry live, at a figure he then restated inconsistently, which is evidence the product genuinely lacks this rung.
